domain.name: fnv
domain.one_line: Sequential ordering under a martingale (MMFE) demand signal: place N orders while demand information is progressively revealed, realize demand at the horizon, and sell against cumulative inventory to maximize expected profit.

N.source: §3 (p.474): 'The planning horizon consists of N + 1 periods, from 1 to N + 1. The first N periods are ordering periods, representing N ordering options available to the newsvendor at different times.' N is general in the model; N = 3 is this study's design value.

mmfe_mode.domain: categorical: 'additive' | 'multiplicative' — which forecast-adjustment link the theory is instantiated with
mmfe_mode.source: §3 (p.474): 'We consider both additive and multiplicative MMFE that differ in how forecasts are adjusted.' Both links are part of the theory and are carried through the same formulas via I_n; they are separate instantiations, never two draws of one uncertainty.

order.source: §4.1 (p.475): 'The decision in period n is Q_n, a nonnegative order quantity.' The recursion maximizes over x_n >= x_{n-1}, so the only restriction the model places on an order is that it cannot be negative — no capacity limit and no ceiling appear anywhere in the model.

c_order.domain: real sequence c_1..c_N; the model requires only 0 < c_1 < c_2 < ... < c_N < r (strictly increasing, all under the price)
c_order.source: §3 (p.474): 'Let c_n be the cost of ordering one unit in period n. We assume 0 < c1 < c2 < ... < cN < r, i.e., it is cheaper to order earlier.' The ORDERING is the model structure. The arithmetic ladder c_n = c1 + (n-1)*lamb that this study renders is one admissible sequence among many, so c1 and lamb are DESIGN constants, not model quantities. Deterministic and known at time 0 by assumption — a model with uncertain purchasing cost (Gurnani and Tang 1999, reviewed in §2) is a different problem.

r.domain: real > 0, and above every ordering cost (r > c_N)
r.source: §3 (p.474): 'The retail price, denoted by r, is exogenously given.' r > c_N rides on the same assumption line as the cost ordering: a period with c_i >= r 'can be eliminated as the newsvendor would never order in that period.'

mu.domain: real — the location of the initial forecast: E[D] under the additive link, and the mean-adjusted log-location under the multiplicative one
mu.source: §3 (p.474): 'Let mu = D_1 be the expected demand in period 1' (a-MMFE); under m-MMFE 'mu = log D_1 - sum_i sigma_i^2/2 [is the] expectation of the logarithm of demand in period 1'. Known at time 0.

signal.domain: independent forecast adjustments, one per epoch, normally distributed with per-epoch variance sigma_i^2 > 0; the variances are free and need not be equal, and no relation among them is imposed
signal.source: §3 (p.474): a-MMFE adjustments are 'independent and normally distributed with mean 0 and variance sigma_i^2'; m-MMFE adjustments are normal with mean -sigma_i^2/2 and the same variance, so the mean-adjusted cumulative information I_n is a mean-zero martingale under either link. The FREE variance schedule is the model statement; deriving sigma_i from a total std and an epoch spacing (this study's stdev and t_last, a Brownian information flow) is a design choice and narrows it.

demand.domain: a random variable on [0, inf) realizing once, at the end of the horizon; given the information state it is normal (additive link) or log-normal (multiplicative link) with location mu + I_n and residual variance sum_{i>n} sigma_i^2
demand.source: §3 (p.474-475): 'Market demand D is a random variable and realizes in period N + 1'; 'the estimate of D after observing I_n under a-MMFE (respectively, m-MMFE) is normal (log-normal) with parameters (mu + I_n, sigma_tilde_n^2)'. DERIVED: it is the terminal value of the forecast process and carries no randomness of its own, so it makes no independent stochastic claim — all of it enters through `signal`.

inventory.domain: real >= 0, unbounded above — the cumulative quantity ordered so far, non-decreasing
inventory.source: §4.1 (p.475): 'x_{n-1} is the inventory state tracking the total number of units ordered before period n (with x_0 = 0)'. DERIVED from the decisions: it accumulates orders and nothing else, so it makes no independent stochastic claim.

information.domain: real, unbounded in both directions — the cumulative mean-adjusted forecast adjustment, starting at 0
information.source: §4.1 (p.475): 'I_n is the information state representing the up-to-date information about forecast adjustments (with I_1 = 0)'. DERIVED: it is the running sum of `signal`, so it makes no independent stochastic claim.

out_of_scope: salvage value for unsold inventory, any penalty for unsatisfied demand beyond the lost margin, and discounting — §3 (p.474): 'There is no salvage value for unsold inventory, no penalty for unsatisfied demand, and no discounting.' The undiscounted objective is why the discount factor is 1.0

fixed (setup) ordering costs and order cancelations — §3 (p.474): 'although we assume no fixed ordering costs and cancelations in our model, our results can be extended to include these under certain conditions'; that extension lives in the paper's online supplement and is not part of this model
explicit inventory holding costs — §3 (p.474): 'We do not explicitly consider inventory holding costs that might be incurred for the goods ordered; they can be easily embedded into ordering costs'

delivery lead time and the risk of not receiving an order in time: every order placed in an ordering period is available at the selling season with certainty. Wang and Tomlin (2009), reviewed in §2, is the model that adds a stochastic lead time
the single-ordering restriction the paper analyses in its §4.2 and §5: choosing WHEN to place one order is a different decision problem, not a special case of this one
the multiple-forecaster, asymmetric-information generalization of Oh and Ozer (2012) — §1 (p.473) states this is the single-forecaster special case
dynamics: event order inside ordering period n (§4.1, p.475): observe I_n, review the position x_{n-1}, order q_n >= 0 and incur c_n * q_n, raise the position to x_n = x_{n-1} + q_n
forall n in 1..N: x_n = x_{n-1} + q_n, with x_0 = 0 and q_n >= 0 — orders accumulate and are never returned (the recursion maximizes over x_n >= x_{n-1})
forall n in 1..N: the cost incurred in period n is c_n * q_n, with the sequence c_n strictly increasing in n
forall n in 2..N+1: I_n = I_{n-1} + adj_n, with I_1 = 0 and E[adj_n | history through n-1] = 0 once the multiplicative link's mean shift is absorbed — the forecast process is a martingale
forall n in 1..N: given I_n, D is normal (additive link) or log-normal (multiplicative link) with location mu + I_n and residual variance sigma_tilde_n^2 = sum_{i=n+1}^{N+1} sigma_i^2
in the selling season (§4.1, p.475): D realizes once, and revenue r * min(D, x_N) is collected
objective: maximize E[ r * min(D, x_N) - sum_{n=1..N} c_n * q_n ], undiscounted

notation.N: N — the number of ordering periods; the horizon is N + 1 periods (§3, p.474)
notation.Q_n: order — the order quantity placed in period n (§4.1, p.475)
notation.x_n: inventory — cumulative units ordered through period n, x_0 = 0 (§4.1, p.475)
notation.I_n: information — the cumulative mean-adjusted forecast adjustment, I_1 = 0 (§3-§4.1, p.474-475)
notation.D: demand — market demand, realized in period N + 1 (§3, p.474)
notation.c_n: c_order — rendered by this study as c1 + (n-1)*lamb; the model asks only for 0 < c_1 < ... < c_N < r (§3, p.474)
notation.r: r — the exogenous retail price (§3, p.474)
notation.mu: mu — mu = D_1 under a-MMFE, mu = log D_1 - sum_i sigma_i^2/2 under m-MMFE (§3, p.474)
notation.sigma_i: signal — the std of the period-i forecast adjustment; rendered by the derived constant signal_stdevs (§3, p.474)
notation.sigma_tilde_n: the residual uncertainty after period n, sigma_tilde_n^2 = sum_{i=n+1}^{N+1} sigma_i^2 (§3, p.475); it is what the myopic safety stock is priced against
notation.S_n(I_n): the optimal base-stock level: mu + I_n + b_n under a-MMFE, exp(mu + I_n + b_n) under m-MMFE (Proposition 2, p.475)
notation.b_n: the safety-stock offset, the solution of g_n(y_n) = 0 in equations (6)-(7); independent of the forecast evolution (Proposition 2, p.475)

constants.name: N
constants.desc: number of ordering periods (= horizon T); paper default 3

constants.name: stdev
constants.desc: total demand std dev; the per-period signal schedule signal_stdevs is derived from it and the epoch spacing

constants.name: t_last
constants.desc: time location of the last ordering epoch (paper T, in (0,1)); renamed from T to avoid the reserved horizon symbol. Sets the epoch spacing tau and thus signal_stdevs.

constants.name: lamb
constants.desc: ordering-cost increment per period: rate at period n is c1 + (n-1)*lamb

constants.name: c1
constants.desc: ordering cost per unit in period 1 (paper default 1.0)

constants.name: mu
constants.desc: additive MMFE: mean demand (E[D] = mu + I, E[I]=0)

constants.name: mmfe_mode
constants.desc: MMFE link selector (categorical): 'additive' -> D = mu + I, 'multiplicative' -> D = exp(mu + I). Selects the terminal link ONLY (the demand-signal family is the same normal-increment MMFE either way) — a constant-conditioned dynamics expression, not an uncertainty candidate. The base scenario is 'additive'; the 'mmmfe' instance selects 'multiplicative' (and, independently, widens stdev to 0.2). Read by the R-event demand update and passed straight through to FnvScenario.mmfe_mode by the adapter.

constants.name: signal_stdevs
constants.desc: DERIVED, pre-resolved per-period signal volatility (length N+1): signal_stdevs[n] = sqrt(tau[n+1]-tau[n]) * stdev, tau = concat([0], linspace(0, t_last, N), [1]). Baked as exact float reprs so the interpreter's normal draw matches the domain's bit-for-bit; the domain re-derives it from stdev/t_last/N (see assumptions_log).

constants.name: order_max
constants.desc: DERIVED, pre-resolved per-scenario order ceiling: the ~5-sigma demand ceiling, order_max = mu + 5*stdev (additive) or exp(mu + 5*stdev) (multiplicative). Upper bound of the `order` decision. With no salvage value, ordering past the highest plausible demand is strictly dominated -- the marginal unit cannot be sold -- so this is the useful action scale, not a safety margin. Baked per scenario like signal_stdevs because the link is mode-dependent and bound entries name a constant rather than carry an expression; an instance that changes mu, stdev or mmfe_mode must re-bake it (the 'mmmfe' instance does). Matches FnvEnv's action_space high exactly, so the IR bound and the gym bound derive from one argument.

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current ordering period n (1-indexed, 1..N); the horizon ends after the order at period N

state_variables.name: inventory
state_variables.desc: cumulative quantity ordered so far (sum of past decisions); non-decreasing, sold against realized demand at the horizon

narrowed.by: implementation:the gym's observation box — the model leaves the accumulated position unbounded above

state_variables.name: information
state_variables.desc: I[period]: cumulative demand-signal information revealed so far (the MMFE martingale); observed by the agent before each order

narrowed.by: implementation:the gym's observation box — the model leaves the information state unbounded in both directions

state_variables.name: total_cost
state_variables.desc: sum of ordering costs incurred so far; subtracted from terminal revenue to give profit

narrowed.by: implementation:the gym's observation box — the running bill is unbounded above in the model

info_fields.name: cost
info_fields.desc: ordering cost incurred this period = (c1 + (period-1)*lamb) * order

info_fields.name: demand
info_fields.desc: realized demand at the horizon: mu + information (mmfe_mode='additive') or exp(mu + information) (mmfe_mode='multiplicative'); 0 until the terminal period

info_fields.name: sales
info_fields.desc: units sold at the horizon = min(demand, inventory); 0 until the terminal period

decisions.name: order

type.rationale: order quantities are continuous non-negative reals in the MMFE ordering problem

bounds.rationale: Overrides the derived literal [0, 3]. That bound was reasoned from the ADDITIVE branch only ('mu=1, stdev<=0.3, so ~3 covers the useful action scale'), but the IR also carries a multiplicative instance whose own action ceiling is exp(mu + 5*stdev) = 7.39 -- so the differential drew decisions from [0, 3] while the domain's reachable range ran to 7.39, leaving everything above 3 unverified on that instance. Naming the scenario constant `order_max` makes the bound resolve per instance and match the gym's action_space high in both branches.

decisions.desc: quantity ordered this period; adds to cumulative inventory. Consumed by the _mdp layer; the gym action_modes are agent-facing encodings.

narrowed.to: [0, order_max], the per-instance ~5-sigma demand ceiling (1.5 additive / 7.389056 multiplicative)
narrowed.by: design:order_max — with no salvage value an order past the highest plausible demand is strictly dominated, so this is the useful action scale + implementation:the gym's Box action space, which names the same constant

ammfe.desc: mean-zero MMFE increment revealed at period n; std = signal_stdevs[n], the pre-resolved per-period volatility schedule (see assumptions_log). Observed, not latent — it enters `information`.

updates: demand = (mu + information) if mmfe_mode == 'additive' else exp(mu + information)

per_step_components.name: ordering
per_step_components.desc: per-step ordering cost as a (negative) profit contribution

per_step_components.name: revenue
per_step_components.desc: terminal sales revenue r*min(demand, inventory); 0 until the horizon (sales==0). Episode total = -total_cost + revenue = profit.

invariants.name: inventory_accumulates_orders
invariants.desc: the only inflow is the period's order; nothing leaves before the horizon

invariants.name: cost_accumulates
invariants.desc: running procurement cost is the sum of per-period order costs

invariants.name: demand_is_terminal_only
invariants.desc: demand realizes once, at the horizon; every earlier row reports 0

invariants.name: sales_capped_by_stock
invariants.desc: at the horizon the firm sells the lesser of demand and what it accumulated

action_modes.name: order
action_modes.desc: identity: the agent sets the order quantity directly, clipped to the non-negative box.

reward_modes.name: profit
reward_modes.desc: per-step objective.total = ordering + revenue = -cost each period, plus terminal sales revenue (sense=maximize, no sign flip). Episode sum = profit.

requires_memory.rationale: fully observed: the MMFE signal is revealed into `information`, so (inventory, information, period) is the sufficient statistic; no hidden latent

obs_normalization.rationale: inventory, information, and orders_to_go sit on modestly heterogeneous scales; spec §8.3 says normalize

assumptions_log: MMFE INFORMATION PROCESS: demand information arrives as a martingale (Heath & Jackson 1994 MMFE). The increment revealed at period n is mean-zero normal with std signal_stdevs[n]; cumulative information I[period] is observed before each order, and demand realizes at the horizon as D = mu + I (additive) or D = exp(mu + I) (multiplicative), selected by the categorical `mmfe_mode` constant.

DERIVED SCHEDULE BAKED AS DATA: signal_stdevs[n] = sqrt(tau[n+1]-tau[n]) * stdev with tau = concat([0], linspace(0, t_last, N), [1]) is scenario construction (domain-side). The IR carries the *resolved* schedule as exact float reprs so the interpreter's normal draw matches the domain's FnvScenario.signal bit-for-bit; instances that change stdev/t_last/N would need a re-resolved schedule (FNV's parameter variety lives in the design grids, exercised by conformance, not this differential).

1-INDEXED HORIZON: the N=3 ordering periods run on a 1-indexed clock (1..N); the interpreter terminates when the post-increment clock reaches horizon.T, so the terminal clock value is N+1 = 4 (horizon.T = 4, not N). The demand-signal seed key uses period directly (1..N), matching the domain's state.period, so trajectories diff bit-exactly under seed scheme v2 ([period, source_id, 1, episode_seed, seed_salt]).

TERMINAL REALIZATION: demand and sales are realized under the `period == N` guard (event R), before the period increment; they are 0 on every non-terminal row. Objective total = -cost + revenue accumulates to profit = revenue - total_cost.

MMFE LINK IS A CONSTANT SELECTION: additive (D = mu + I) and multiplicative (D = exp(mu + I)) use the same demand-signal family (the `signal` slot's generator is identical); they diverge only in the deterministic terminal link, applied once at the horizon in the R event. That link is not an uncertainty candidate but a constant-conditioned dynamics expression, keyed on the categorical `mmfe_mode` constant ('additive' | 'multiplicative'). The base scenario is 'additive'; the 'mmmfe' instance selects 'multiplicative' AND independently widens the signal (stdev 0.1 -> 0.2, with the derived signal_stdevs schedule re-baked to match) — showing both a mode selector and a derived-constant re-bake under one instance override. Both are differentially verified by the covering-set sweep (--all-instances): base = aMMFE, instance mmmfe = mMMFE.

DESIGN GRIDS (PARAMETER SWEEPS) OUT OF IR SCOPE: the mode is now in-IR (the `additive` selector), but the aMMFE / mMMFE parameter sweeps (stdev x t_last x lamb ranges) remain experiment-design grids (spec §5.6), consumed only by training/eval drivers. The IR formalizes concrete scenarios (base + instances); grid coverage is verified structurally by the conformance harness.

ORDER BOUND IS THE 5-SIGMA DEMAND CEILING: the `order` decision's upper bound is the scenario constant `order_max` = mu + 5*stdev (additive) / exp(mu + 5*stdev) (multiplicative), re-baked per instance. Rationale: with no salvage value an order beyond the highest plausible demand is strictly dominated, so this is the useful action scale. Replaces the literal [0, 3], which was derived from the additive branch alone and silently under-covered the multiplicative instance in the differential (reachable to 7.39). Bound entries name a scenario constant rather than carry an expression, which is why the mode-dependent link is resolved at bake time; gym.action_modes names the same constant so the model bound and the agent-facing encoding cannot drift.

OBSERVATION CARRIES THE SCENARIO CONSTANTS: the `vec` mode is [stdev, t_last, lamb, period, inventory, information] -- the three scenario constants first, then the clock and the two physical state variables, matching FnvEnv._get_obs exactly. The constants are present because one policy is trained across a whole design grid (spec 5.6) and must condition on which cell it is in: the optimal offsets b_n move substantially with stdev, t_last and lamb, so a policy blind to them cannot be optimal grid-wide -- it can only learn one compromise action over all 540 cells. `period` is carried raw rather than as the derived orders_to_go = N - period + 1; the two are bijective for fixed N, so this is an encoding choice and the code's encoding wins. Corrects an earlier 3-feature list [inventory, information, orders_to_go] that the implementation never emitted; no gate caught the divergence because the differential verifies the mdp layer and never reads the observation.

MODEL / DESIGN / RENDERING SEPARATED (2026-08-17, spec §5.0 at v0.9.5): `mdp.model` now states the theory at the paper's own generality, which moved the freeze token once — see §IR-CHANGELOG F2. Three renderings that had read as model statements are now on the record as design choices: (i) the cost ladder — the paper assumes only 0 < c_1 < ... < c_N < r, so the arithmetic c_n = c1 + (n-1)*lamb is one admissible sequence and `lamb` is a design constant with no counterpart in the model; (ii) the volatility schedule — the per-epoch variances sigma_i^2 are FREE in the model, and deriving them from a total `stdev` and an epoch spacing `t_last` (a Brownian information flow) is this study's design; (iii) the action ceiling — the model bounds an order only below, at 0, so `order_max` is a design cap and carries a `narrowed` citation rather than reading as a capacity the theory states. Nothing about the executable rendering changed: the structural fingerprint is unmoved and the differential still MATCHes on both instances.

benchmarks.name: prop2
benchmarks.basis: the paper's Proposition 2: the safety-stock offsets b_n are the solution of the one-dimensional recursion (6)-(7), which is independent of the forecast evolution, and S_n(I) = mu + I + b_n (log-linear under m-MMFE). EXACT as an algorithm — it IS the paper's characterization of the optimum, not an approximation of it. The numerical caveats are the quadrature and the root-find tolerance in solving g_n(y_n) = 0. Held deliberately independent of `dp`: their agreement is the spec §1.2 second-implementation gate, and if they ever diverge the bar itself is in question.

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: value-function DP on the reduced state z = x - (mu + I): backward induction over a grid, with extrapolating interpolation below the maximizer and an interior-argmax guard (a clamped lookup silently emits 'never order' offsets — see the traps). EXACT as an algorithm: it solves the paper's recursion (1)-(2) directly. The numerical caveats are the grid step and the truncation of the normal tail. Agrees with `prop2` to a paired mean of 1e-07 in scored profit, max 2.4e-05 over all 540 cells, against a per-cell eval SE of ~0.004.

benchmarks.name: myopic
benchmarks.basis: myopic safety stocks b_hat_n = sigma_tilde_n * Z_{beta_n} with beta_n = (r - c_n)/r, applied at every period: each period is priced as a one-shot newsvendor against the uncertainty that still remains, ignoring the option to order again later. Feasible by construction — it runs under the real information set. The paper's Corollary 1 gives b_n <= b_hat_n, so it over-orders early by construction, which is what makes it the must-beat baseline rather than a serious contender.

benchmarks.name: fitted
benchmarks.basis: the §14.2 readback scored as a policy: a trained net distilled into per-cell offsets b_hat_1..b_hat_N from its own trajectories, then run under the identical CRN protocol as every other arm. Feasible by construction. It REFUSES any cell where the policy never acts (b_hat_n is unidentifiable there), so its coverage is a subset of the grid — 209/540 on a-MMFE, 508/540 on m-MMFE — and its number is not comparable cell-for-cell with a full-grid arm.

tier2.structure: the state-dependent base-stock policy of Propositions 1-2: S_n(I) = mu + I + b_n, log-linear under m-MMFE, with an offset b_n that does not depend on the forecast evolution
tier2.claim: The learned policy implements the paper's optimal form — it orders up to a level that moves one-for-one with the information state (one-for-one in logs on the multiplicative branch), with a per-period offset.
tier2.instrument: Stage-5 readback on the policy's own trajectories, ACTING periods only and one fit per grid cell (q = max(0, S - x) is censored at zero, so a non-ordering period identifies no level); the slope against I, plus the fitted offsets scored as a policy on the same CRN block under §14.2
